LESSON: TIME, DISTANCE, AND SPEED

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.4 Volume and Capacity (8 lessons) • metre cube (m3 ) as a unit of
Topic 3.5: Time, Distance, and Speed

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Time, Distance, and Speed. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify units of measuring time in real- life situations
2. identify speed as distance covered per unit time in different situations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: TIME, DISTANCE, AND SPEED
Time, Distance, and Speed is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Time, Distance, and Speed problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Time, Distance, and Speed question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Time, Distance, and Speed question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Time, Distance, and Speed set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Time, Distance, and Speed.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Time, Distance, and Speed in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify units of measuring time in real- life situations
2. identify speed as distance covered per unit time in different situations

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
